order_note: No predecessor and no order on this engine. SQL 141 (owner decision 2026-11-03: the platform owner creates permanent vendor organizations; a tenant enters a vendor's Partner Code to add that vendor as a payee, immediately, without the vendor approving; the code never creates a tenant partnership and never shares a check, a claim or any other record) needs public.tenants (id, name, partner_code, subscription_status), public.tenant_users (tenant_id, user_id), public.tenant_partner_code_aliases (tenant_id, code), auth.uid(), public.aws_user_tenant_ids(), public.is_platform_owner() and the roles checksops and authenticated, and an applying login that reads public.tenants and public.tenant_partner_code_aliases without row security (it owns them with no FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or is a superuser or BYPASSRLS); the file itself raises sql141_prerequisite_missing or sql141_definer_cannot_read (55000) otherwise, before any change. It creates public.vendor_tenants and public.tenant_vendor_payees (both new; RLS on, not forced; one SELECT policy each TO authenticated; every non-owner grant revoked, the default privileges of a new table included, the cause of SQL 117's staging rollback fixed in SQL 118, then SELECT only to checksops and authenticated) and three SECURITY DEFINER functions, aws_vendor_payee_add(uuid, text), aws_vendor_payee_remove(uuid, uuid) and aws_platform_owner_set_tenant_vendor(uuid, boolean), EXECUTE checksops and the owner only. public.tenants (columns, triggers, grants, rows), tenant_partnerships, shared_checks, stakeholder_accounts, external_payment_recipients and every existing policy and function (lookup_tenant_by_partner_code and aws_tenants_member_column_guard included) are not changed. Nothing moves money, creates a Moov account or reads one; the send endpoint accepting a vendor payee link (aws/functions/api/providers/production/moov-send.mjs) is a separate API change, not in this file. If the read-only inspect finds both tables, both policies and the three functions as intended it reports already_applied true and nothing is applied (the pin is then recorded as verified live, not applied). No later migration replaces these objects.

tooling.note: Guarded tooling for SQL 141: sql141-permanent-vendor-payees-production-apply.mjs --inspect (read-only) and the receipt-gated --apply on the engine shared with the staging guarded executor (choice sql141-permanent-vendor-payees); production-sql-one-shot.mjs --migration sql141. intended_replacement_sha256 is the code-derived fingerprint (releaseIntendedHash in release-sql-state.mjs, equal to the staging pin's): the three functions as the file defines them (plpgsql, VOLATILE, SECURITY DEFINER, result jsonb, search_path public and row_security off, the body hashes, EXECUTE exactly checksops and the owner), the two SELECT policies TO authenticated, and the two new tables (columns, constraints, indexes, RLS on and not forced, the policy and trigger lists, table ACL exactly authenticated SELECT and checksops SELECT besides the owner). The pre-conditions refuse a table, policy or function of the same name in any other shape, a missing prerequisite, and a login that cannot read public.tenants and public.tenant_partner_code_aliases past row security (definer_can_write_relations, the file's own sql141_definer_cannot_read rule); every other object in schema public is in the unrelated-catalog snapshot and must be unchanged. The tooling does not authorize anything: this pin stays execute false until a reviewed change records the staging acceptance, the production inspect and an owner approval.
